title: KV + Prefix Cache Telemetry — metric draft notes (working)
content:
Context
- Sprint goal: make cache behavior observable + actionable with low overhead and safe cardinality.
- We need a consistent story across:
  (a) prefix cache (prompt/prefix reuse, more “string/prompt identity”)
  (b) KV cache reuse (token-level reuse in attention cache; impacted by batching + scheduling)
- We also need to support SRE/operator questions: “why did unit cost increase yesterday?” and “is this real or telemetry drop?”

Terminology (as used in runtime today)
- Prefill: compute for prompt tokens / initial context.
- Decode: iterative token generation.
- Prefix cache: mapping from (canonicalized prompt features) -> cached prefill artifacts (implementation detail varies).
- KV cache: attention key/value tensors resident on GPU that can be reused when next request shares prefix tokens.
- Reuse depth: number of tokens in request that were served from cache before we had to prefill.

High level: what we want to measure
1) Hit-rate (but defined carefully):
   - Token-weighted (how many tokens avoided compute) is more meaningful than request-weighted.
   - Must handle partial hits (e.g., 300 tokens reused out of 800).
2) Miss reasons:
   - If we can’t tell “policy off” vs “evicted” vs “hash mismatch” vs “version mismatch” then hit-rate by itself isn’t actionable.
3) Pressure / eviction signals:
   - Hit-rate dips can be due to memory pressure or workload shift; need pressure gauge + evictions.
4) Wasted prefill:
   - Prefill tokens computed that didn’t contribute to later reuse (regression signal; helps quantify cost of bad locality).

Draft metric candidates (names are placeholders; Nadia/Telemetry will enforce final naming)
A) Core counters (token-weighted)
- kv_cache_reused_tokens_total
  - Increment by count(reused prefix tokens) for each request.
  - This is the “numerator” for token-weighted KV reuse.
- kv_cache_requested_prefix_tokens_total
  - Increment by count(prefix tokens eligible for reuse) for each request.
  - Denominator depends on definition of “eligible” (see open questions).
- kv_cache_missed_tokens_total
  - Increment by count(prefix tokens not reused) when reuse_depth < eligible_prefix_tokens.
  - Might be derivable from requested - reused, but explicit helps avoid subtle drift.

B) Request-level counters (request-weighted)
- kv_cache_requests_total
  - Total requests processed (at the point we know reuse stats).
- kv_cache_requests_full_hit_total
  - Reuse depth == eligible_prefix_tokens.
- kv_cache_requests_partial_hit_total
  - 0 < reuse_depth < eligible_prefix_tokens.
- kv_cache_requests_miss_total
  - reuse_depth == 0 (or eligible_prefix_tokens==0 ? needs clarity).

C) Histograms / distributions
- kv_cache_reuse_depth_tokens_bucket
  - Histogram of reuse_depth tokens per request.
  - Useful for seeing shifts in reuse depth (many requests with 1-20 reused vs 500+ reused).
- prefix_cache_reused_tokens_bucket
  - Similar histogram but scoped to prefix cache layer (if distinct from KV layer).
- prompt_length_tokens_bucket
  - Probably already exists; we can tag other metrics by prompt bucket rather than emit a separate metric.

D) Miss reason taxonomy (counter)
- kv_cache_miss_events_total{reason=...}
  - Proposed reasons (early draft):
    - capacity (no cache space / allocation fail / memory pressure forced skip)
    - evicted (entry existed but was evicted before reuse)
    - ttl_expired (entry expired by TTL policy)
    - policy_disabled (route config disables caching, or request opted out)
    - hash_mismatch (prompt canonicalization mismatch, tokenization mismatch, or different prompt bytes)
    - version_mismatch (model version differs from cached entry)
    - schema_mismatch (rare: cache format/version mismatch across runtime versions)
    - unknown (fallback bucket)
  - Important: keep taxonomy stable; do not add per-week “new reasons” that break dashboards.

E) Eviction / pressure
- kv_cache_evictions_total{reason=...}
  - reasons: lru, ttl, memory_pressure, compaction, manual_clear (if supported)
- kv_cache_memory_bytes (gauge)
- kv_cache_memory_limit_bytes (gauge)
- kv_cache_memory_pressure_ratio (gauge)
  - pressure = memory_bytes / limit_bytes, clamped [0, 1.5] maybe.
- kv_cache_eviction_age_seconds_bucket
  - How long entries lived before eviction (if available cheaply).

F) Wasted prefill (draft; be careful)
- wasted_prefill_tokens_total
  - Definition attempt: tokens prefilled for a request that would have been eligible for reuse but were recomputed due to miss/eviction/etc.
  - Equivalent-ish to kv_cache_missed_tokens_total *when* those missed tokens actually incurred prefill compute (but under batching/continuous prefill, attribution gets tricky).
- wasted_prefill_requests_total
  - Count requests where wasted_prefill_tokens > 0.

Labels/tags (draft) — cardinality constraints noted
We need metrics sliceable by how Redwood operates:
- model_id (allowlisted short ID, not full path)
- model_version_id (maybe allowlisted; risk: high churn)
- route_id (strong need, but must be allowlisted / hashed stable mapping)
- deployment_mode (hosted|dedicated|private)
- region (e.g., us-east-1)
- tenant_tier (free|pro|enterprise?) possibly from gateway
- prompt_length_bucket (coarse, e.g., [0-128, 129-256, 257-512, 513-1k, 1k-2k, 2k+])
- request_type (chat|completion|embedding?) — for cache probably only chat/completion
- streaming (true|false)

Explicitly avoid (or gate behind sampling)
- tenant_id raw (cardinality explosion)
- exact route path string
- request_id/session_id
- user_id
- prompt hash as label

Metric computation notes / where to hook
- We only know reuse_depth once we attempt to attach to cache during prefill planning.
- For streaming: retries + reconnect can cause double counting if we emit at “request start” and then retry. Prefer emitting at a single “finalized reuse stats” point (or guard with idempotency key).
- For continuous batching: reuse depth might be computed per request, but prefill work is shared; wasted_prefill attribution per request is potentially misleading.

Open questions (capture from runtime chats)
1) What is the correct “eligible_prefix_tokens” definition?
   - Option A: eligible = prompt_tokens - system_tokens? (no, too product-specific)
   - Option B: eligible = tokens before first divergence in token IDs between request and cache key.
   - Option C: eligible = prompt_tokens up to a configured max_reuse_tokens cap.
   - Concern: if eligible includes tokens that we never intended to cache (e.g., over size limit), we’ll show a fake “miss”.

2) Token-weighted vs request-weighted: which is the primary hit-rate?
   - Proposal: publish both, but dashboards default to token-weighted.
   - Token-weighted tells cost impact; request-weighted tells user experience distribution.

3) Prefix cache vs KV cache: do we need separate hit-rates?
   - If prefix cache is just a policy layer feeding KV, then separate metrics may confuse.
   - But operators need to distinguish:
     - “we matched the prefix identity but KV allocation failed” (prefix hit, KV miss)
     - “we never matched identity” (prefix miss)

4) Multi-turn chat attribution
   - If request contains conversation history, reuse depth should treat the entire prompt as the unit.
   - If conversation includes timestamps / non-deterministic fields, canonicalization can help but must be privacy-safe.
   - Question: do we treat reused tokens from same session differently than cross-session reuse? (Probably not for v1; just measure reuse.)

5) Streaming retries / partial responses
   - If a stream is retried mid-flight, do we count it as a new request? If so, reuse stats likely differ.
   - Proposed: record a label retry=true and/or count retries separately, OR ensure metrics are emitted only once per “logical request” from gateway.
   - Need to align with gateway semantics (Ethan/Amara).

6) Batched prefill correctness
   - We can compute “reused tokens” per request, but “wasted prefill tokens” could be inflated/deflated if prefill is shared.
   - Potential approach: treat wasted_prefill as “missed eligible tokens” rather than literal extra GPU work. But naming must reflect that.

7) Where does eviction reason come from?
   - Runtime currently knows “evicted due to pressure” vs “ttl” vs “lru”.
   - But a miss may not know if it missed due to eviction unless we can detect “would-have-hit key existed recently”. Might require an optional debug map (too expensive?).
   - Pragmatic approach: miss reasons separate from eviction reasons; only attribute eviction when you can be certain.

Sampling / overhead (draft)
- Counters are cheap; high-frequency per-token events are not.
- Emit per-request aggregated numbers (reused_tokens, eligible_tokens, miss reason) instead of per-token events.
- For histograms, keep bucket count low; avoid p99-level buckets.
- Consider sampling for:
  - detailed miss reason breakdowns
  - reuse_depth histogram (if too heavy)
- Default in prod: 1.0 for core counters, <1.0 for histograms if needed. Marcus to confirm with perf.

Cardinality guardrails (runtime-side ideas)
- Route/model labels should use short stable IDs from gateway allowlist, not arbitrary strings.
- If label value not recognized: set to "other" or "unknown".
- If route_id missing: set "unattributed".
- Potentially emit two metric families:
  - high-level (no route_id)
  - per-route (sampled, allowlisted)

Proposed initial acceptance tests (for ENG-4821/4822)
- Repeated identical prompt => reuse_depth increases to ~prompt_len (after warmup), reused_tokens_total increments, miss reasons drop.
- Different prompt => reuse_depth=0, miss reason hash_mismatch (or "no_match").
- Same prompt, different model_version => miss reason version_mismatch.
- Cache disabled at route => miss reason policy_disabled; eligible tokens should be 0 or excluded (TBD).
- Force eviction via tiny cache => evictions_total increments; hit-rate drops; pressure ratio ~1.
- Streaming retry simulated => counters not double counted (or explicitly counted in retry bucket).

Notes from brainstorming (raw)
- “Hit-rate” should not be a single number; we need a bundle: hit-rate + miss reasons + pressure.
- Keep metrics names stable; dashboards depend on it; do naming once after ADR.
- Don’t emit prompt hash label. If we need to debug prompt canonicalization, do it via traces (span annotations) not metrics.
- Wasted prefill might be the most valuable operator metric, but also most likely to be wrong. Prefer shipping it behind a flag until validated.

Next steps (as of Mar 12)
- Omar/Samir: align on eligible_prefix_tokens definition and where to compute it in request lifecycle.
- Nadia/Logan: confirm metric naming + required labels + bucket scheme.
- Ethan/Amara: finalize route_id/model_version_id propagation to runtime context.
- Marcus: perf canary runs at sampling=1.0 core counters, evaluate histograms cost.
- Schedule a 30m review with SRE (Sean/Allison) on which 3-5 panels must be correct on day 1.

Appendix: example derived metrics (for dashboards)
- kv_token_hit_rate = sum(kv_cache_reused_tokens_total) / sum(kv_cache_requested_prefix_tokens_total)
- kv_request_hit_rate = sum(kv_cache_requests_full_hit_total) / sum(kv_cache_requests_total)
- partial_hit_share = sum(kv_cache_requests_partial_hit_total) / sum(kv_cache_requests_total)
- miss_reason_share(reason) = sum(kv_cache_miss_events_total{reason}) / sum(kv_cache_requests_total)
- wasted_prefill_ratio = sum(wasted_prefill_tokens_total) / sum(prompt_tokens_total)  (prompt_tokens_total may come from existing request token counters)
